summary: AVGO at $380 has hit the preferred entry zone from yesterday's report — a technical selloff dragged by broad chip rotation, not a fundamental change. Q2 beat EPS $2.44 vs $2.32 (Jun 3). Q3 AI revenue guided +200% YoY to $16B. The $35B Apollo/Blackstone AI infrastructure platform (Jun 9) with Anthropic validates AVGO as the custom chip + networking backbone of the AI buildout. JPMorgan calls investors 'aggressive buyers at current levels', PT $580.

catalysts.name: Q3 AI Revenue +200% YoY — $16B Guide
catalysts.description: Broadcom guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue >$16B (vs ~$5B same quarter 2025) — 3× acceleration. Earnings Sep 3, 2026. Beat-and-raise cycle intact.

catalysts.name: Apollo/Blackstone $35B AI Platform with Anthropic
catalysts.description: Broadcom, Apollo, and Blackstone launched a $35B AI infrastructure platform (Jun 9) — financing 20+ GW of global AI deployment using AVGO custom chips. Secures multi-year revenue visibility.

catalysts.name: New Hyperscaler XPU Design Win
catalysts.description: Management signaling a 4th major hyperscaler adding AVGO custom XPU — expected announcement H2 2026. Each new customer expands the $60–90B 2027 TAM estimate.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Rate cuts benefit VMware debt servicing (saves ~$1.5B/yr) — incremental FCF expansion. Not the primary driver but a tailwind.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Software-heavy revenue mix (VMware ARR ~$8.5B) insulates from materials inflation. Semiconductor margins stable at ~65% gross margin.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Broad semis selloff weighs on AVGO short-term but does not affect the $16B AI revenue run-rate or custom XPU design wins — those are long-cycle contracts.
macroRisk.summary: Low macro sensitivity. AI custom silicon + VMware ARR creates a durable revenue base that is largely immune to rate and inflation cycles. The current -3% is sector noise.
